title: God, in the Gospel of His Son
description: God, in the Gospel of His Son in Tonic Solfa to WINCHESTER NEW, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Benjamin Beddome wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 192 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “The Gospel Revelation”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to WINCHESTER NEW; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: God, in the Gos-pel of his Son, Makes his e-ter-nal coun-sels known; 'Tis here his rich-est mer-cy shines, And truth is drawn in fair-est lines.

lines: God, in the Gospel of his Son,
And truth is drawn in fairest lines.
To form our minds, to cheer our hearts;
Its influence makes the sinner live;
It bids the drooping saint revive.
And comfort yields to contrite souls;
It brings a better world in view,
And guides us all our journey through.
May this blest volume ever lie
Close to my heart, and near my eye,
Till life's last hour my soul engage,

licence: Public domain: Benjamin Beddome died in 1795.
credits: Words by Benjamin Beddome (1717–1795), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to WINCHESTER NEW by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
